tests: A chart carrying information available nowhere else in the document. Tests whether the pipeline recognises that a chart needs a long description rather than a short alt text.
adversarialFeatures: the chart is inline SVG, so its text labels are extractable as page text rather than being locked inside a raster image
the per-quarter series appears nowhere else, so the chart is not redundant decoration
three series distinguished partly by colour and partly by dash pattern
legend is positioned below the axis label and out of visual reading order
title: Throughput Trend Analysis

figures.adjacentProse: Northern rises steadily across all four quarters. Southern is flat within noise. Coastal declines slowly and continuously, and is the only series that ends below where it began.
figures.correctAccessibleTreatment: Requires a long description conveying all three trends and the axis ranges, not a short alt text. The adjacent prose is a legitimate extraction source and covers the trends but omits the axis ranges and the values.

expectedOutcome: A short alt text such as 'a line chart' is a WCAG 1.1.1 failure with better grammar. Correct results are either a long description extracted from the adjacent prose, or NEEDS_REVIEW.
intentionalProblems: chart content is not available in a table anywhere
SVG text labels may be recovered as loose page text and mistaken for body content rather than figure internals
